item.title: GDB Debugging: From Core Dumps to Live Processes
item.description: Master GDB for debugging C/C++ programs — set breakpoints, inspect memory, analyze core dumps, and attach to live processes for production debugging.

item.title: Linux Memory Debugging: From vmstat to Memory Leaks
item.description: Learn how Linux reports memory usage through vmstat, free, /proc/meminfo, and /proc/vmstat. Cover transparent hugepages, OOM killer, memory cgroups, and how to diagnose memory leaks in production.

item.title: Linux /proc Filesystem: A Deep Dive into Process Information
item.description: Explore the Linux /proc filesystem to monitor processes, inspect memory, CPU info, and understand how tools like ps and top read kernel data.

item.title: Paxos Consensus Algorithm: How Distributed Systems Reach Agreement
item.description: A deep dive into the Paxos consensus algorithm—prepare phases, accept phases, multi-Paxos, and why Google Spanner, CockroachDB, and Neo4j use it for distributed agreement.

item.title: Rate Limiter System Design: How to Build a Distributed Defense Against API Abuse
item.description: Design a rate limiter from token buckets to distributed Redis clusters. Cover the algorithms, architecture, and trade-offs that protect APIs at scale from abuse and cost overruns.

item.title: ClickHouse Architecture: How a Column-Oriented Database Processes Billions of Rows
item.description: A deep dive into ClickHouse's architecture—vectorized execution, MergeTree storage, and how it achieves sub-second queries on trillion-row datasets.

item.title: DNS Deep Dive: How Domain Name Resolution Actually Works
item.description: A thorough look at DNS — recursive vs iterative queries, record types, DNSSEC, DoH/DoT, TTL behavior, and why your cache matters more than you think.

item.title: eBPF: Linux's Most Powerful Observation Framework
item.description: What eBPF is, how it works, why it matters compared to kernel modules, and practical tools like bpftrace, tcpdump -B, and execsnoop.

item.title: Raft Consensus Algorithm: How Distributed Systems Agree on Reality
item.description: A deep dive into Raft's leader election, log replication, and safety guarantees—and why etcd, CockroachDB, and TiKV all rely on it for distributed consensus.

item.title: strace: Debugging Linux System Calls Like a Pro
item.description: Learn how strace works under the hood, how to read its output, and how to debug real-world Linux problems with it.

item.title: URL Shortener System Design: How to Handle Millions of Redirects Per Second
item.description: Design a URL shortening service like bit.ly or TinyURL from scratch. Cover hash techniques, distributed storage, redirect latency, and the architecture that handles millions of requests per day.

item.title: TCP/IP Internals: How a Packet Travels Across the Network
item.description: A deep dive into the TCP/IP protocol stack, from application data to physical frames, and everything that happens in between.

item.title: Linux Process Management: Understanding ps, top, and htop
item.description: Linux process model, /proc filesystem, ps, top, htop, process states, signals, zombie and orphan processes, CPU and memory metrics, and how the kernel tracks running programs.

item.title: SQL Indexing: A Deep Dive into Database Performance
item.description: B-tree and composite indexes, covering indexes, partial indexes, EXPLAIN plan analysis, and how to diagnose and fix slow SQL queries with real examples.

item.title: Database Normalization: When to Normalize and When to Denormalize
item.description: Database normalization forms (1NF-3NF), when to denormalize for read performance, OLTP vs OLAP design patterns, star schemas, and practical guidelines for balancing integrity and speed.

item.title: PostgreSQL vs MySQL in 2024: A Practical Comparison
item.description: PostgreSQL vs MySQL: data types, JSONB, ACID, replication, MVCC, query planner, extensions, and cloud support compared for real production workloads.

item.title: Database Transactions and Isolation Levels Explained
item.description: ACID properties, Read Uncommitted to Serializable isolation levels, dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads, pessimistic vs optimistic locking, deadlock handling, and race condition prevention in SQL databases.

item.title: Redis Beyond Caching: Using Redis as a Primary Database
item.description: Redis data structures (hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams), persistence options (RDB/AOF), pub/sub, rate limiting, and when to use Redis as a primary database instead of just a cache.
